chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), that he said:

By Allah, Ali (peace be upon him) would eat the food of a slave and sit as a slave sits. He would buy two Sanbulani shirts and give his servant the better one, then wear the other. If the sleeve exceeded his fingers, he would cut it, and if it exceeded his ankle, he would shorten it.

He ruled for five years without placing a brick upon a brick, nor a mud-brick upon a mud-brick, nor granting any land, nor bequeathing a silver or gold coin. He would feed the people wheat bread and meat, then return to his home and eat barley bread with oil and vinegar.

Whenever two matters were presented to him, both pleasing to Allah, he would take the one that was harder on his body. He freed a thousand slaves from the toil of his own hands, by which his hands became dusty and his face sweated. No one among the people could bear his deeds, even as he would pray a thousand units of prayer day and night.
The person who most resembled him was Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), yet no one among the people could bear his deeds after him.

key_terms.آجرة: Baked brick — symbolizing he did not build any structure for himself
key_terms.أكل العبد: The food of a slave — eating the simplest and humblest food, a mark of asceticism
key_terms.السنبلانيين: Sanbulani — a type of simple, coarse shirt, said to be from Sanbalan region (Roman-style garments)
key_terms.بيضاء ولا حمراء: White (silver) nor red (gold) — meaning he left no wealth whatsoever
key_terms.كد يده: The toil of his hand — indicating he freed slaves using money earned through his own manual labor
key_terms.لبنة: Mud-brick — emphasizing he did not even use the simplest building materials for himself

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali live during his caliphate according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) gives a vivid and detailed account of Imam Ali's (AS) ascetic lifestyle during his caliphate. Despite being the ruler of the Muslim world for five years, Ali (AS) lived with extreme simplicity — eating like a slave, giving his servant the better garment, feeding others wheat bread and meat while eating barley himself, never building a home or accumulating wealth, freeing a thousand slaves from his own labor, and praying a thousand units daily. This portrayal was delivered in the context of teaching the early Shia community what true Islamic leadership looks like, contrasting Ali's conduct with worldly rulers.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from `Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Najran from `Asim b. Humayd from Muhammad b. Qays from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as). He said:

By Allah, `Ali (as) would eat the food of a slave and sit as a slave sits. He would buy two Roman shirts and give the better one to his servant and wear the other. If the sleeve exceeded his fingers, he would cut it, and if its end would exceed his heel, he would shorten it.

He ruled for five years, yet he did not put a brick atop a brick [on his own house], nor a tile atop a tile, nor acquire a piece of land, nor bequeath a silver or gold coin. He would feed the people bread and meat, then he would go to his house and eat barley, oil, and vinegar.

He would not be given two options that Allah is pleased with except that he would take the one that was harder on his body. He freed one thousand slaves with the money he earned with sweat on his face and effort by his hands. None from the people could bear his deeds, even if he would pray one thousand units day and night.
Even the person that resembled him the most – `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) – could not bear his deeds, nor could anyone of the people after him.
